title: Musk vows affordable Starlink in India days before Ambani’s record Jio IPO
source_used: The Business Times (Singapore), text credited to Reuters
key_facts: Elon Musk wrote on X on Saturday 10 Oct 2026 that SpaceX will need to price Starlink affordably in India, or no one will buy it.
He named no prices; mobile data in India costs about US$0.08 a gigabyte, among the lowest in the world.
He said competition would benefit the average Indian citizen and that Ambani's profits would be lower but he is not going out of business.
Jio Platforms, which owns Reliance's telecom arm, is days from India's largest-ever IPO, targeting a valuation of US$106 billion.

Musk has accused Prime Minister Modi's government and Ambani of stalling Starlink's entry; India's government denies bias and says all three satellite ventures, including Jio's own, await final security clearance.
On Friday night Musk taunted Ambani as 'Prime Minister Ambani'; Reliance has not responded to requests for comment.
SpaceX also plans to enter the mobile carrier market itself, starting in the US.
quote_evidence: “Obviously, if Starlink is too expensive in India, no one will buy it, so SpaceX will need to make pricing affordable,” he said in a post on his social media platform X on Saturday (Oct 10).

“The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambani’s profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business,” Musk added.
India’s government has denied any bias in its approval process, noting that the three satellite ventures seeking to launch, including Starlink’s and Jio’s, are all awaiting final security clearance.
why_it_matters_hint: A price pledge for people in India, where Starlink has no launch date, and pressure on Jio before its record share sale.
notes: Follow-up of the Musk-Ambani row.
